title: Tanzanian Fish and Chips
community: Urban Tanzania — the universally loved street food
author: Chef Jabir
desc: Tanzanian Samaki na Chips — crispy spiced-battered tilapia alongside thick-cut masala chips. Tanzania's most beloved street food combination — the batter is spiced with Tanzanian curry powder, the chips tossed in masala. Better than the British original.
longDesc: Samaki na chips is the street food of Tanzania's cities — at every corner, vendors fry fish and chips side by side. The Tanzanian version is better because the batter is spiced and the chips are tossed in masala spice.
steps: Make spiced batter: combine flour, baking powder, spices. Whisk in cold water. Rest 5 minutes.
Soak potato chips in cold water 20 minutes. Dry thoroughly.
First fry chips at 160°C for 6—8 minutes. Remove.
Dip fish in spiced batter. Fry at 180°C for 4—5 minutes per side.
Second fry chips at 180°C for 3—4 minutes until golden.
Toss chips immediately in masala spice mix.
chefTips: Double-frying chips is the secret to crispiness.
Masala spice on hot chips — heat blooms the spices.
cookingScience: Double frying: first fry gelatinises starch inside; second fry at higher temperature creates rapid Maillard browning on the drier exterior. Dramatically crispier than single-fry.
sustainabilityTips: Local Tanzanian fish and locally grown potatoes.
culturalNote: Samaki na chips is the food that urban Tanzania runs on — the evening meal of students and workers across every city.
